title: Chapter 95: All School Uniforms
html:
“No photographs or filming once you’re inside. There are four scenarios: the Sealed Classroom, the Fifth Restroom Cubicle, the Pen Spirit, and the Deep Well. Each contains clues to the exit, so you’ll have to experience all four to escape.” Chen Ge checked their waivers several times. He had a feeling the forms would soon prove useful.

“This isn’t our first Haunted House. We know the rules.” Fei Youliang adjusted his glasses and peered inside. “At least the atmosphere isn’t bad.”

“Then I won’t waste my breath.” Chen Ge had planned to introduce each scenario, but they clearly needed no explanation. “Follow me.”

Chen Ge led the two men to the first-floor entrance of Night of the Living Dead. They surveyed the dilapidated set and its shabby mannequins.

“This place is ten years out of date.”

“With sets like these, I should sue you for overcharging us.”

Zhu Jianing and Fei Youliang wandered into the Night of the Living Dead scenario and touched the dust that had gathered on the mannequins. “Just how long has this place been deserted?”

“Looks like the business is dying. I should’ve known you hired the same paid trolls to fill the reviews with praise.”

“Are you two done?” Chen Ge raised the wooden boards from the floor. “The entrance is here.”

“It’s underground?” Unfazed, the two men left Night of the Living Dead and stopped before the descending staircase.

The dark corridor plunged into an abyss. Classroom doors creaked on either side, and before they even reached the stairs, a cold wind rose from below and brushed their skin.

“Now… this is… better.”

As the two young men entered the Mu Yang High School scenario, Chen Ge yelled from the entrance, “If you’re really afraid, yell for help at the cameras—the workers will come help you.”

After replacing the boards, Chen Ge remembered that Mu Yang High School had neither surveillance cameras nor a proper exit. The warning had come from habit alone. I’d better follow them. Hopefully, they’ll still be sane when I catch up.

He left Xu Wan at the entrance to manage the line, donned the Doctor Skull-cracker costume, and switched the background music to Black Friday. Then he entered Mu Yang High School carrying the box of name tags Fan Yu had given him.

…

Zhu Jianing and Fei Youliang lingered near the entrance until Chen Ge closed the boards. Then they exchanged a signal, took wireless cameras from their backpacks, and clipped them to their chests.

“Each of us will record our side. We’ll film everything inside his Haunted House, and after we solve it, we’ll post the guide online.”

“Will that achieve anything?”

“For a local Haunted House like this, the sets and mechanisms are trade secrets. They need mystery to attract visitors. Once a guide appears online, the experience loses its appeal—that’s why they ban cameras.” Fei Youliang adjusted his camera and took the lead. “We’ll edit the footage to look as boring as possible, post it, then hire paid commenters to bury him in bad reviews.”

“Okay.” Zhu Jianing looked around. “Still, the man put real effort into the set. It does feel like an abandoned high school.”

“It’s still fake. Compared with the 3D horror films I’ve seen, this is nothing.” Fei Youliang sounded bored rather than frightened. “Let’s get it over with.”

They advanced through the dim corridor between rows of empty classrooms. Doors creaked on their hinges, and strange noises drifted from the darkness within.

“Do you think the exit will be inside these two classrooms beside the entrance? After all, the comments did say that the boss is a master manipulator.”

“That’s your first mistake. Obsess over the exit and you’ve already fallen into his trap.” Even as he spoke, Fei Youliang kept his torso level. Both men were experienced cameramen.

“You’re right. Thankfully, you came with me.”

“In reality, Haunted Houses are very boring. It’s just people scaring people, and if you take it too seriously, you lose.”

The dark corridor seemed endless. Despite their bravado, they advanced at a glacial pace. Scorch marks covered the walls, and the stale air carried the distinctive odor of burning.

As living humans entered the scenario, the atmosphere inside Mu Yang High School slowly changed. In an unseen corner, many pairs of eyes slowly opened.

A lifelong horror-film enthusiast, Fei Youliang remained unmoved by the authentic setting. The muscular Zhu Jianing fared worse. He wilted under the pressure, hiding behind his companion while his gaze darted toward every dark corner.

The background music was not frightening by itself, yet it quickened his pulse and disrupted his breathing. When Fei Youliang stopped abruptly, Zhu Jianing walked straight into his back.

“What’s wrong?” Zhu Jianing asked, unaware that his voice had fallen to a whisper.

“This classroom is different.” Fei Youliang stood outside the sealed room. The dark uniforms filling its chairs gave him the uncanny impression of a class in session.

“It’s full of uniforms.” Even more frightened than Fei Youliang, Zhu Jianing shivered after one glance through the window. “Should we try somewhere else first?”

“Don’t panic. One of the employees is probably hiding inside. That’s why it looks different.” Fei Youliang managed to retain his composure. “The owner said we had to experience four scenarios, and this must be one of them. It’s a major feature of the Haunted House, so we need to record it, solve it, and post the footage.”

As he spoke, the door slowly swung open, moved by an invisible hand.

“There must be some kind of control mechanism. It’s common equipment used in the shooting of scary movies.” Fei Youliang slapped Zhu Jianing on his arm. “Come on, let’s go catch some ghosts.”

“You’re right, but…” Cold sweat beaded across Zhu Jianing’s forehead. “I’ve looked everywhere. There are only uniforms in there—nowhere for a person to hide.”

“There’s probably some hidden compartment. Be careful. This means that the actor might come out to scare you from unexpected corners.” Fei Youliang and Zhu Jianing dawdled outside the classroom for a long time before finally entering it.
